\chapter{Communication Complexity — One Way}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.CommunicationComplexity.DeterministicCC.OneWay
\section{Overview}

This module develops one-way deterministic communication protocols, in which Alice sends
a single message from a finite codebook and Bob produces the output.  The main results
relate the one-way communication complexity of a function to its standard (interactive)
deterministic communication complexity, with an additive $\lceil \log_2 |\alpha| \rceil$
overhead for Bob to transmit the decoded output.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[One-way deterministic protocol]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.Protocol}
\statementsource{roughgarden-cc-oneway}{pdf-043896d6545f-p002-b003}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.Protocol}
\leanok
A one-way deterministic communication protocol for inputs $x \in X$, $y \in Y$, and
output type $\alpha$ is a structure consisting of a finite, nonempty \emph{message
codebook} \texttt{Message}, Alice's encoder $\mathtt{send} : X \to \mathtt{Message}$
that selects a codeword from the codebook based solely on her input, and Bob's decoder
$\mathtt{decode} : \mathtt{Message} \times Y \to \alpha$ that produces the final output
from the received message and his own input.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Protocol execution]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.Protocol.run}
\statementsource{roughgarden-cc-oneway}{pdf-043896d6545f-p002-b003}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.Protocol.run}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.Protocol}
Given a one-way protocol $p$ and inputs $x \in X$, $y \in Y$, executing the protocol
yields the output $p.\mathtt{decode}(p.\mathtt{send}(x),\, y) \in \alpha$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Protocol bit cost]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.Protocol.cost}
\statementsource{roughgarden-cc-oneway}{pdf-043896d6545f-p002-b004}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.Protocol.cost}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.Protocol}
The communication cost of a one-way protocol $p$ is $\lceil \log_2 |\mathtt{Message}| \rceil$
bits, where $\mathtt{Message}$ is the protocol's codebook.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Protocol computes a function]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.Protocol.Computes}
\statementsource{roughgarden-cc-oneway}{pdf-043896d6545f-p002-b003}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.Protocol.Computes}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.Protocol, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.Protocol.run}
A one-way protocol $p$ \emph{computes} a function $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$ if
$p.\mathtt{run}(x, y) = f(x, y)$ for every pair of inputs $(x, y)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Embedding into the finite-message model]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.Protocol.toFiniteMessage}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.Protocol.toFiniteMessage}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.FiniteMessage.Protocol, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.Protocol}
Given a one-way protocol $p$ with finite output type $\alpha$, one obtains an interactive
finite-message protocol by having Alice send her one-way message and then having Bob
encode the decoded output as an index in $\{0,\ldots,|\alpha|-1\}$ and transmit it.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Embedding into the finite-message model preserves output]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.Protocol.toFiniteMessage_run}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.Protocol.toFiniteMessage_run}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.FiniteMessage.Protocol.run, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.Protocol, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.Protocol.run, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.Protocol.toFiniteMessage}
\difficulty{1}
Let $p$ be a one-way deterministic communication protocol over input types $X$, $Y$ and
a finite, nonempty output type $\alpha$, and let $x \in X$ and $y \in Y$. Then executing
the finite-message protocol obtained from $p$ by the embedding into the finite-message
model on the inputs $x$ and $y$ yields the same element of $\alpha$ as executing $p$
directly on $x$ and $y$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Complexity of the finite-message embedding]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.Protocol.toFiniteMessage_complexity}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.Protocol.toFiniteMessage_complexity}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.FiniteMessage.Protocol.complexity, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.Protocol, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.Protocol.cost, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.Protocol.toFiniteMessage}
\difficulty{1}
Let $p$ be a one-way deterministic communication protocol with inputs in $X$, $Y$ and
output type $\alpha$, and suppose $\alpha$ is finite and nonempty. The finite-message
protocol obtained from $p$ — Alice sends her one-way message, after which Bob transmits
the decoded output as an index in $\{0,\ldots,\abs{\alpha}-1\}$ — has communication
complexity
\[
\left\lceil \log_2 \abs{\mathrm{Message}} \right\rceil + \left\lceil \log_2 \abs{\alpha}
\right\rceil,
\]
that is, the bit cost of $p$ plus $\lceil \log_2 \abs{\alpha}\rceil$, where
$\mathrm{Message}$ is the codebook of $p$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[One-way communication complexity]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.communicationComplexity}
\statementsource{roughgarden-cc-oneway}{pdf-043896d6545f-p002-b004}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.communicationComplexity}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.Protocol, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.Protocol.Computes, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.Protocol.cost}
The one-way deterministic communication complexity of $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$ is the
infimum (in $\mathbb{N}_\infty$) of the bit costs $p.\mathtt{cost}$ over all one-way
protocols $p$ that compute $f$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Cost bound for one-way communication complexity]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.communicationComplexity_le_iff}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.communicationComplexity_le_iff}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.Protocol, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.Protocol.Computes, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.Protocol.cost, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.communicationComplexity, CommunicationComplexity.Internal.enat_iInf_le_coe_iff}
\difficulty{1}
Let $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$ be a function and let $n \in \bbn$. The one-way
deterministic communication complexity of $f$ is at most $n$ if and only if there exists
a one-way deterministic protocol $p$ that computes $f$ and whose bit cost satisfies
$\mathrm{cost}(p) \le n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Lower bound characterization of one-way communication complexity]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.le_communicationComplexity_iff}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.le_communicationComplexity_iff}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.Protocol, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.Protocol.Computes, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.Protocol.cost, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.communicationComplexity}
\difficulty{1}
Let $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$ be a function and let $k \in \bbn$. Then $k$ is at most the
one-way deterministic communication complexity of $f$ (as an inequality in
$\bbn_\infty$) if and only if every one-way deterministic protocol that computes $f$ has
bit cost at least $k$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[One-way bound implies interactive bound]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.deterministic_communicationComplexity_le_of_oneWay_le}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.deterministic_communicationComplexity_le_of_oneWay_le}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.FiniteMessage.Protocol.complexity, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.FiniteMessage.Protocol.run, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.Protocol.Computes, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.Protocol.cost, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.Protocol.run, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.Protocol.toFiniteMessage, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.communicationComplexity, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.communicationComplexity_le_iff, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.communicationComplexity, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.communicationComplexity_le_iff_finiteMessage}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$ be a two-argument function whose output type $\alpha$ is
finite and nonempty, and let $n \in \bbn$. If the one-way deterministic communication
complexity of $f$ is at most $n$, then the (interactive) deterministic communication
complexity of $f$ is at most $n + \lceil \log_2 \abs{\alpha} \rceil$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[One-way bound implies deterministic bound for Boolean functions]
\lean{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.deterministic_communicationComplexity_le_of_oneWay_le_bool}
\label{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.deterministic_communicationComplexity_le_of_oneWay_le_bool}
\leanok
\uses{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.communicationComplexity, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.OneWay.deterministic_communicationComplexity_le_of_oneWay_le, CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.communicationComplexity}
\difficulty{3}
Let $X$ and $Y$ be the input types of Alice and Bob, and let $f : X \to Y \to
\mathrm{Bool}$ be a two-party Boolean-valued function. If the one-way deterministic
communication complexity of $f$ is at most $n$ for some $n \in \bbn$, then the
(interactive) deterministic communication complexity of $f$ is at most $n + 1$.
\end{theorem}
